Linear describes itself as a product development system for teams and agents.
Karri reported that the app shows a spinner forever during iOS startup, making it look like the car disappeared.
Jori asked Linear to take a stab at the issue.
Linear created the issue via Slack on behalf of Karri.
Linear is designed for workflows shared by humans and agents, including drafting PRDs and pushing PRs.
Linear is described as being purpose-built for modern teams with AI workflows at its core.
Intake and integrations automatically turn conversations and customer feedback into actionable issues that are routed, labeled, and prioritized for the right team.
Didier said the team is still blocking initial render on a full vehicle_state sync every time.
Andreas suggested rendering sooner, loading the rest in the background, and tracking startup timing.
Planning and monitoring helps teams plan and navigate from idea to launch with initiatives, roadmaps, and up-to-date PRDs.
AI and automations lets teams build and deploy AI agents that work alongside people or take over entire issues end to end.
Cursor added retry handling for failed image uploads to an issue.
ChatPRD drafted complete offline mode requirements and broke the work into sub-issues.
Build, review, and ship helps teams streamline code reviews with clear diffs, better context, and fewer back-and-forth comments.
HomeScreen renders a loading spinner until isFullySynced is true, then shows the dashboard with vehicle state.
HomeScreen shows a loading spinner only while syncStatus is PENDING, then renders the dashboard with sync status.
CodeReview is shown with Diff.Provider and several components, including Slow, Fragmented, HumanOnly, Frictionless, Integrated, and AgentReady.
The changelog announces new Slack and GitHub loop triggers, letting loops start from Slack and GitHub changes and be shared as templates.
Linear Agent can be assigned a task, then works in a secure cloud environment to write and test code before opening a pull request for review.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams, and they can respond to changes in initiatives, projects, and cycles, edit Linear documents, and post updates to Slack.
Linear says it powers over 40,000 product teams, from startups to major enterprises.
The Free plan costs $0 and includes unlimited members, 2 teams, 250 issues, the Agent platform, and Linear Agent.
The Basic plan costs $10 per user per month, billed yearly, and adds 5 teams, unlimited issues, unlimited file uploads, admin roles, and Loops.
The Business plan costs $16 per user per month, billed yearly, and adds unlimited teams, private teams and guests, Triage Intelligence, Code Intelligence, Linear Insights, Linear Asks, and Zendesk…
The Enterprise plan has custom pricing with annual billing only and adds invoice/PO billing, SAML and SCIM, granular admin controls, enterprise-grade security, advanced org modeling, migration and…
The pricing page says the Enterprise plan is trusted by more than 40,000 companies.
Linear Docs gives an overview of Linear's features, integrations, and how to use the app.
The docs include popular guides for Start Guide, Import Issues, Projects, and GitHub Automations.
The Workflows guide explains how to create new statuses and design custom issue workflows.
Linear Docs includes guides for Select Issues, Issue Relations, Display Options, Triage, Parent and Sub-Issues, Notifications, and Teams.
Issue Relations lets you mark issues as blocked, blocking, related, or duplicate.
Triage is a special inbox for issues from integrations and other teams.
The Gong integration automatically creates Linear issues from Gong call recordings.
The integration is available to workspaces on the Enterprise plan.

Each Gong-created issue includes a drafted title and description, transcript excerpts with speaker attribution, and a link to the exact moment in the recording where the request or problem was raised.
Linear periodically checks Gong recordings and only includes customer-facing conversations, skipping internal or private calls and recordings under 10 minutes.
The integration filters out non-actionable items such as sales-related questions, beta access requests, general inquiries, and internal commentary.
Actionable findings are created as issues in Linear and added to the team's Triage view for review and backlog management.
To set up Gong, you go to workspace Settings > Integrations, search for Gong, then enable recording intake in Gong and choose the team that should receive Gong-generated issues.
